title: [storage] the storage page names the scratch that landed objectives left behind, by agent and objective, from the scratch walk the serve already does
prompt:
Spawn, objective 232 [storage] (the lead's pick of 2026-11-19 14:1x, "A + B, B is the contract", from rev-g's storage survey sync/survey-storage-rev-g/README.txt; author rev-g; readers rev-b first, rev-h second): the storage page names the scratch that landed objectives left behind, by agent and objective.

Why. The storage north star, bytes a landing leaves behind, read 682 MB against 50 MB on 11-18, and scratch was all of it (+41.3 GB of 38.2 GB over 56 landings).
- The survey (13:54, extents): 43.1 GB of scratch is reviewers' per-objective trees, about 32.7 GB of them of objectives already landed, and 20.4 GB of that cargo build output. The figure says how much, never whose.
- The fleet rule from today (the lead, 14:1x): every tree is claimed (`spawn scratch claim`, objective 140) with its objective and build path ".../target", and a reviewer removes its trees when the objective lands. Objective 145's sweep catches build output that is forgotten.
- This objective makes that rule visible: the walk the serve already does lists every claimed folder with whether its objective landed (objective 140's `scratch.claimed[].landed`). Nothing adds them up, so the storage page never says that 15 GB of 4/222 is still on disk, or whose it is.

What changes:
- A storage diagnostic, storage.landed_scratch_bytes, "Scratch of landed objectives", unit bytes, last in the storage page's diagnostics (after the six of objective 176, and after leaked test schemas while it is shown). No range: it is never out, never an alert figure, never on a line, and no gate, integrator or deploy step reads it (core-line metrics are monitoring only).
  - Its value: over the reading's claimed folders whose objective landed (the same `landed` pairs scratch_json uses), each folder's bytes, or its build_bytes while its lease runs (objective 155 never walks a leased folder whole: then only its build output is known). A folder of an objective not landed, or with landed unknown, adds nothing; an unclaimed folder is never counted, whatever its name.
  - A landed claimed folder whose lease ended also counts in storage.unowned_scratch_bytes (reason "lease ended"): the two overlap and are never added together.
  - Its by_owner: one row per agent and objective, {agent, objective, bytes, folders, leased}, leased being how many of the row's folders were counted by their build output only; largest bytes first, then agent, then objective.
  - With no folder claimed: 0 and by_owner []. With no scratch reading yet, no complete walk in it (no roots, no walk within storage.scratch_bound yet, or a root refused: the states where storage.unowned_scratch_bytes is null), or the landings not readable: null, with a note saying which, never 0 (R2: rev-h's F1, rev-b).
- The Home card (web/src/coreLines.ts and CoreLines.tsx): the diagnostic's own mark, as every diagnostic; and coreLinesView's new `landedScratch`, one row per by_owner row, name "<agent> · <objective>", text "<size> · <n> folder" or "folders", then " · <k> leased, build only" when k > 0, shown under the storage line beside the claimed folders.
- Cost: no new store read and no new file walk. The claimed folders, their bytes and build bytes come from the kept scratch reading (unowned::now), and the landings from the one claimed_landed read lines_at already makes; the figure is computed from those in memory.

Owner part: rsi/scenarios/232.sh (new), rsi/backlog/232.json (new), and rsi/scenarios/176.sh, two checks of the diagnostics' number and order: (3) "the diagnostics, in order" gains storage.landed_scratch_bytes last, and (5)'s card model counts 7 diagnostics, not 6 (176's scratch has no claimed folder, so it reads 0).

Tests (unit): the sum and rows from a reading with a landed walked folder, a landed leased one (build bytes only), a folder of an objective not landed, landed unknown (null pairs: null and the note), no complete walk (unowned none, or a root refused: null and the note), and none claimed (0, []); the rows' order with ties on bytes, one between agents and one between two objectives of the same agent (R2: rev-h's and rev-b's F2). Web (web/test/coreLines.test.ts): the empty card's expected view gains landedScratch: [] (R2: rev-b's F3), and landedScratch's words for a row with and without leased folders. The adopted set's diagnostics list gains the key last. Like every figure, it counts in observability.not_measured while it has no value (a reading with no scratch walk).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/232.sh, black box, a real `spawn serve` on its own database with objectives 1/7 and 1/9 landed and 1/8 not, and a scratch root of claimed folders:
- (1) storage.landed_scratch_bytes is the last diagnostic, no range, state no_range, on no line, never an alert figure; its value is a + d (1/7, released, walked whole) + sess/q (1/9, released) + sess/o's build output only (1/9, leased); not b (1/8), not sess/o's sources, not t007 (unclaimed);
- (2) by_owner: rev-e 1/007, rev-i 1/007, rev-e 1/009 (2 folders, 1 leased), largest first, each row exact;
- (3) the card's words: the mark "Scratch of landed objectives" and its size; landedScratch's names and texts;
- (4) a root with nothing claimed: 0 and [];
- (5) read only: nothing under the root changes;
- (6) no complete walk, each null with a note, never 0: the first walk past storage.scratch_bound, no roots, the one root refused by an exclude that holds it, and by a symlink;
- (7) rev-e's two landed objectives with equal bytes, 1/9 claimed before 1/7: the rows read 1/007 then 1/009.
On live main aaa1b740, 232.sh exits 1 (no such diagnostic), and 176.sh as changed exits 1.

Verified by: after landing, on live, GET /api/core-lines' storage.landed_scratch_bytes and its by_owner match the claimed folders of landed objectives in scratch.claimed (the same answer), and fall when a reviewer removes its landed trees (the lead's or rev-g's look).
